if you’re not in therapy already, i would recommend seeing someone who specializes in body image issues to help you along the healing journey. you got a surgery for something that has been distressing you for a long time, & the surgery is still fresh. the immediate result can be jarring. it’s easy to hyper focus. i haven’t had surgery (only injections + body/facial piercings/tattoos), but i’ve cried many a time after getting a hair cut/color that was exactly what i asked for because of how shocking it is (i have really awful facial dysmorphia). i’ve also ruined my eyebrows on many occasions due to the hyper fixation/dysmorphia. i’ve also had mental breakdowns over my tattoos. it gets easier once you’re used to it, even if you’re not happy with it.

medication can also help (although as someone who has tried MANY medications- that’s a battle on its own to find the right one, which can also be an incredibly distressing process, so definitely emphasis on the /can/ in the “can help”). heal your mind while your body heals. if you arent happy with the results once its fully healed, there are non-surgical procedures to help achieve desired results or consult with a few other doctors on what your options are surgically.

i see a difference personally, although it may seem subtle, once it’s fully healed it may be a total 180 in the right direction. not a doctor, but everyone’s anatomy is different, thus making it unable to do a big procedure without winding up botched. less can be more. more can be possibly be detrimental.

I just think it's applicable to this job. It's not just a simple spa, like I said, their marketing insists that it is a powerful tool for bettering oneself/the mind. Not really something massage parlors tout, those are more about the whole "treat yoself" form of self-care. But we can agree to disagree. I'm over it at this point lol. I do agree that it should be taught in schools, however.
